result.title: Gaussian Process Bandits for AI System Optimization with Selectively Verified Feedback
result.summary: Gaussian process bandits exploit similarities among configurations to optimize prompts, retrieval systems, and agent workflows. In these applications, however, inexpensive model-based evaluations can disagree with trusted task outcomes. We study selective verification when an action is chosen before a diagnostic is observed and trusted feedback is informative on an unknown set of diagnostic states. A finite reliability class and a finite RKHS signal dictionary describe these two sources of uncertainty. We construct a fixed audit design that combines reliability coverage with reward separation and establish a finite-time regret bound that accounts for a hard audit budget and the rounds needed to obtain informative observations. A safe adaptive extension mixes this robust design with predictable Chernoff allocations while preserving a uniform identification floor and exact expected acquisition-cost accounting. For signed-coordinate kernels, structured and diffuse reliability classes require different audit scales despite sharing the same reward geometry. Synthetic experiments distinguish these certified designs from an adaptive posterior heuristic and GP controls. Safe adaptive allocation reduces aggregate regret relative to the fixed design under the exact dictionary, but its finite-budget error certificate is numerically loose. Conditional-feedback errors can remove the heuristic's advantage and target perturbations can reverse it. Separate AI-task replays assess feedback correction and fitted-dictionary policies without establishing end-to-end validation of a learned selective-verification method.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究在动作先于诊断观测、可信反馈仅在未知诊断状态子集上有效的设定下，如何用高斯过程 bandit 优化 AI 系统配置：构造结合可靠性覆盖与奖励分离的固定审计设计，给出含硬审计预算的有限时间 regret 界，并提出保留识别下界与精确成本核算的安全自适应分配。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「廉价模型评估与可信结果不一致」及带预算的验证/审计设计，与 LVR 关注的可信证据获取、成本核算和停止决策有概念对应，可用于核查能否迁移为 latent 推理中的证据筛选与验证准则；但仅为较远领域的理论工作，属推测性启发。
